Bird stickers for the world's living bird species

 

 花叔开源的全球鸟类贴纸库：按全球统一鸟类名录AviList整理的1.1万多种鸟，每种一张白边贴纸，附多语种鸟名和分布、形态、保护等级数据。贴纸出自花叔做的观鸟App「鸣迹」。中文说明 →

 See the whole library in use at birdalbum.com. Bird Album is a free bird guide built on these stickers: look up any species by name in 15 languages, see where it lives and which months it is around, and open a map of 8,171 birding hotspots that shows what people are seeing at each one this month.

 New every day: Today in Birds. One short bird story a day, built on these stickers: look-alike pairs and how to tell them apart, what is on the move this season, where a bird's name comes from. In 15 languages, with a new issue every morning (Beijing time).

By Huashu (花叔), from the bird-watching app Mingji (鸣迹). More than 11,000 bird species across 45 orders and 249 families, following AviList v2026, the unified global checklist first published in 2025 (the IOC list has ended in its favour). Every species that AviList does not flag as extinct or possibly extinct is included, plus 43 flagged species that already had a sticker: extinct, extinct in the wild, possibly extinct, or, for two, once extinct in the wild and since reintroduced (see extinctionStatus ). Every species has a sticker. Each species comes with structured data: taxonomy, names in up to 43 languages, cross-database IDs, and what each sticker was made from.

 Version 2.0 moved the taxonomy from IOC 15.2 to AviList v2026. 82 species changed their scientific name (and so their id and sticker path), 91 former species are now subspecies of another species, and 30 new species were split off. Every change is listed in data/crosswalk-ioc15.2-avilist2026.csv , and each record keeps its old IOC ID under previous . See CHANGELOG.

 

 AI-generated, and every file says so. Each sticker file carries XMP/IPTC metadata stating that it is an AI-generated illustration, not a photograph (IPTC Digital Source Type trainedAlgorithmicMedia ), which AI system was used, that it was not verified by experts and may contain errors, the license, and a link back to this repository.

 License in short: the stickers are licensed under CC BY 4.0: use them for anything, including commercial work, editing and redistribution, as long as you credit huashu-bird-sticker with a link to this repository. The data is MIT, and third-party parts are listed in NOTICE.

To look a bird up by name, load data/stickers.json (2.7 MB: scientific, English and Chinese name, file path and the species page on birdalbum.com for each species; the 91 subspecies stickers are listed under forms in data/species.json ). Names in 43 languages are in data/names.csv .

 Bird of the day

A new bird on your GitHub profile, blog or Notion page every day. Paste this line into any Markdown file ( ?lang= for 15 languages, ?theme=dark or auto ):

 

 

 Gallery

Eighteen of the most colourful and distinctive groups, 24 stickers each, picked so that no two look alike. Every sticker shown here meets the quality bar.

 Hummingbirds · Trochilidae — 361 species

 

 Parrots & cockatoos · Psittaciformes — 391 species

 

 Kingfishers · Alcedinidae — 123 species

 

 Bee-eaters, rollers & motmots · Meropidae · Coraciidae · Brachypteraciidae · Momotidae · Todidae — 69 species

 

 Toucans & barbets · Ramphastidae · Capitonidae · Semnornithidae · Megalaimidae · Lybiidae — 132 species

 

 Birds-of-paradise & bowerbirds · Paradisaeidae · Ptilonorhynchidae — 67 species

 

 Pittas · Pittidae — 46 species

 

 Tanagers · Thraupidae — 392 species

 

 Sunbirds & flowerpeckers · Nectariniidae · Dicaeidae — 207 species

 

 Cotingas & manakins · Cotingidae · Pipridae — 120 species

 

 Pheasants & partridges · Phasianidae — 185 species

 

 Ducks, geese & swans · Anatidae — 164 species

 

 Pigeons & doves · Columbidae — 338 species

 

 Waxbills & munias · Estrildidae — 138 species

 

 Jays & magpies · Corvidae — 135 species

 

 New World orioles & oropendolas · Icteridae — 107 species

 

 Hornbills · Bucerotidae — 64 species

 

 Starlings & mynas · Sturnidae — 118 species

 

 One from each order

 

 What's inside

 
 --- --- 
 stickers/ / / .webp One transparent sticker per species with a white outline, about 1,000 px on the long side. . .webp are 91 extra stickers of subspecies that used to be separate species 
 data/species.json One record per species, the complete dataset: taxonomy, names, IDs, range and subspecies, body measurements and ecology, conservation status, sticker and its source. Field reference: data/README.md 
 data/crosswalk-ioc15.2-avilist2026.csv How every IOC 15.2 species maps to AviList v2026: same, renamed, lumped, split 
 data/species.csv The same, flattened for spreadsheets 
 data/names.csv Names in 43 languages (46 columns: Chinese, French and Portuguese each have two variants) 
 data/languages.json Language codes and the IOC multilingual column each one comes from 
 data/field-guide.zh-Hans.json Chinese field-guide notes (look, field marks, sexes and ages, similar species) for 1,596 species, CC BY-SA 4.0 

A record looks like this (names shortened):

 

 Coverage

- Names: English (AviList) covers every species. Other languages come from the IOC multilingual list and are kept only where the species concept did not change; for the 129 species whose boundaries changed (lumps and splits) or that are new, an old name may refer to a different set of birds, so we left it out rather than guess. Simplified Chinese covers 10,947 species (each changed species was checked by hand); French, Spanish, German, Russian, Japanese and Traditional Chinese cover over 94%. Korean, Arabic
